stem: A charge of \(+ 7\ \mu\)C is placed at the centre of two concentric spheres with radius 2.0 cm and 4.0 cm respectively. The ratio of the flux through them will be
Two charges of 1.0 C each are placed one meter apart in free space. The force between them will be

Two point charges of \(+5\ \mu\)C are so placed that they experience a force of \(80 \times 10^{-3}\) N. They are then moved apart, so that the force is now \(2.0 \times 10^{-3}\) N. The distance between them is now
solution: [Textbook misprint — this question has NO correct option as printed, and is therefore withheld rather than keyed. The forces given are \(80 \times 10^{-3}\) N and \(2.0 \times 10^{-3}\) N, a ratio of \(40\); since \(F \propto 1/r^{2}\) the separation grows by \(\sqrt{40} = 6.32\), which is none of the four alternatives. Two different single-digit repairs each rescue the question and each gives a DIFFERENT answer — reading the first force as \(8.0 \times 10^{-3}\) N gives a ratio of \(4\) and "double the previous distance", while reading the second as \(5.0 \times 10^{-3}\) N gives a ratio of \(16\) and "four times the previous distance". Nothing on the printed page decides between them, so no answer is asserted here. (The charge value of \(+5\ \mu\)C is not needed under any reading; the question is a pure ratio.)]
